questions.ask: Run agent-config-kit's iOS quality gate on every pull request (.github/workflows/quality-gate.yml)?
questions.why: Installs a small caller of the kit's ios-swiftui-quality-gate workflow, pinned to one commit: a Linux job runs SwiftLint, the catalog, error-code, suppression and privacy checks, secrets and the skill scan first; only when it passes does a macOS job with Xcode 27 run the whole gate list, the simulator build with a zero-warning count, the tests and the accessibility audit, the String Catalog check against the build, dead code, client drift and the coverage floor. Read-only token, no secrets, and no signing. It needs GitHub Actions; macOS minutes cost about ten times Linux ones on a private repository. An existing quality-gate.yml is kept either way.
questions.detect: the repo is on GitHub (a github.com remote or a .github/ folder); .github/workflows/quality-gate.yml already exists

questions.ask: Review each pull request with DeepSeek, a low-cost paid AI model (.github/workflows/deepseek-review.yml)?
questions.why: Installs a caller of agent-config-kit's reusable DeepSeek review, with notes about this stack: one comment per pull request from a branch of this repository, updated when the repository's owner, a member or a collaborator comments /ask-deepseek. It reads the diff over the GitHub API and runs no pull-request code. It needs the repository secret DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and costs about ten US cents a review at most, usually a cent or two (the diff and the answer are capped); without the secret it passes and sends nothing.
questions.detect: .github/workflows/deepseek-review.yml already exists, or the user has asked for an AI review in CI

questions.ask: Add pull-request templates for work pull requests and dev → prod promotions (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/)?
questions.why: They list only what the gate cannot decide: what a person checks on a simulator, the screens the accessibility audit reaches, the copy in every locale, and the release steps of a promotion. They assume dev and prod branches.
questions.detect: branches dev and prod exist (git branch --list dev prod); .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/ already has files

questions.ask: Do you open several repositories as one Serena workspace (for example this app and the backend whose spec it copies)?
questions.why: Adds .claude/SERENA-WORKSPACE.example.md, which explains how to scope Serena's searches across repos. With a single repo the default needs no documentation.
questions.detect: .mcp.json runs Serena and a .serena/project.yml above this repo lists several folders, or AGENT_WORKSPACE_ROOT is set

questions.ask: Which iOS version is the oldest the app supports?
questions.why: 17.0 is the oldest with Observation and the accessibility audit the rules use, and the oldest Xcode 27 still runs on a simulator; 18.0 or 26.0 drop older devices for newer APIs without #available checks. The seeded files say 17.0: for another answer, set IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET in Config/Base.xcconfig and .iOS(...) in Packages/AppCore/Package.swift to it (the draft repeats this step).
questions.detect: IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET in the .xcodeproj or an existing xcconfig; .iOS(.vNN) in a Package.swift

questions.ask: Which languages does the app ship (en, or en and id)?
questions.why: en,id installs scripts/check/i18n-catalog.json, which makes the String Catalog check require both locales, translated, for every key; list more locales there when the app ships them. en installs nothing: each catalog is then checked against its own source language.
questions.detect: the locales a Localizable.xcstrings already holds, or knownRegions in the .xcodeproj

questions.ask: Does an agent need to read a self-hosted analytics API from this repo?
questions.why: Adds .claude/ANALYTICS.example.md, a template to fill in for that read API. An unfilled template is worse than none, because an agent will try to use it.
questions.detect: the code names an analytics client, or .claude/ANALYTICS.md exists
